selected.rule: Using domain-grouped VALIDATION results only: rank models by phishing F1 at each model's own validation-tuned threshold (F1 reflects both phishing recall and precision). Models within 0.001 F1 of the best are treated as tied; among tied models choose the lowest single-row inference latency, then the smallest file. Test results and raw accuracy are not used.
selected.rule_revision_note: A first draft of this rule (PR-AUC within 0.002 and recall within 0.005 of the best, then fastest) selected Logistic Regression because those tolerances were wider than the real spread between the models and ignored a precision gap on validation. It was replaced by the F1-based rule above before the final run. All three models' test metrics had been printed in the training log at that point.
selected.reason: XGBoost reached validation phishing F1 0.9969 (recall 0.9951, precision 0.9988); it is within 0.001 F1 of the best model and has the lowest latency among those.

stratified.description: Stratified 70/15/15 holdout on de-duplicated URLs. Domains may appear in several partitions, so scores are optimistic.

domain_grouped.description: StratifiedGroupKFold-derived ~70/15/15 split grouped by registrable domain: no domain appears in more than one partition.

shortcut_diagnostics.template_definition: scheme is https, hostname starts with 'www.', and the URL has no path, query or fragment
shortcut_diagnostics.summary: 100.0% of legitimate URLs in the dataset match the https://www.<host> no-path template (phishing: 1.0%), so a one-line rule that predicts 'legitimate' only for that template already reaches accuracy 0.9958 and phishing recall 0.9901 on the domain-grouped test set. Restricted to template-shaped URLs only, the selected model's phishing recall is 0.5745 (precision 0.7642); a model retrained only on those rows reaches recall 0.6028 (precision 0.6204). Headline scores overstate how well the model will do on real legitimate URLs that contain paths, which this dataset does not include.

slices.slice: everything else (has path/query, no www, or http)

manual_probe.note: Ten hand-picked, well-known legitimate URLs scored by the final model. This is a sanity check, not a metric.

limitations: URL-only: no page content, no live reputation, no WHOIS/DNS data.
All legitimate training URLs are https://www.<host> homepages without paths; phishing URLs are far more varied. The model may flag real legitimate URLs that contain paths or lack 'www'.
Domain-grouped results are more conservative than the stratified holdout but still come from one collection of URLs from a limited time window.
Scores are model estimates and were not calibrated against real-world base rates.
